title: Lazur vs Aqua Voice on Mac in 2026: screen-aware dictation or a voice assistant
metaTitle: Lazur vs Aqua Voice on Mac in 2026: which one fits you
description: Lazur vs Aqua Voice on Mac: both read your screen. Aqua dictates on more devices. Lazur also answers, points and guides. Prices from each site.
intro: Lazur and Aqua Voice both read your screen, but they do different jobs. Aqua Voice uses the screen to type more accurately, on Mac, Windows and phones. Lazur uses it to answer questions, point at buttons and guide you through apps, on Mac only. This page compares them on price, privacy, platforms and daily use, using the numbers each site publishes.
tldr: Aqua Voice is an AI dictation app. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Aqua Voice if you want dictation on several devices, or a free plan capped at 1,000 words.
Pick Lazur if you want answers about your screen, spoken aloud, plus help finding buttons.
Lazur Pro is $18/month after a 3-day trial. Aqua Voice Pro is $12/month, or $10/month billed annually.

blocks.text: The difference in one sentence

Aqua Voice reads your screen so it can type what you mean. Lazur reads your screen so it can answer what you ask. Both start with a key you hold while you speak. The difference shows up after you let go. Aqua pastes text at your cursor. Lazur speaks an answer, draws a circle around a button, or walks you through the next click.
What Aqua Voice does well

Aqua Voice is strongest at dictation. Its homepage says it pastes text at the cursor in any app, triggered by holding Space. It refines your text, supports a custom dictionary and writing styles, and lists 49 languages. Max adds Realtime Mode and Voice Commands. Its changelog dates Edit Mode to July 20, 2026, and Realtime Mode to July 26, 2026.

Reviewers mostly praise speed, accuracy and the custom dictionary. On Product Hunt, speed came up 10 times, accuracy 8 times and the custom dictionary 6 times across 16 reviews. That is a small, self-selected sample, so read it as a mood, not a measurement. A reviewer on aestumanda called the custom dictionary a standout feature. SoftOrbits praised its handling of code and technical vocabulary.
What Lazur does that Aqua Voice does not describe

Lazur is built around a question. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on. It does not click for you. You stay in control of every click.

Lazur also handles everyday work by voice. The list covers timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. Longer jobs run in the background. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and comes back with a summary and a report. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on your Mac.
Pricing: what each site charges in 2026

Aqua Voice's pricing page lists a Free plan at $0 to start, with a 1,000-word limit. Pro is $10/month billed annually or $12/month month-to-month, with unlimited words. Max is $19/month billed annually or $24/month month-to-month, and adds Realtime Mode, Voice Commands and Early Access. Business is $19/seat/month billed annually or $24 monthly, with a minimum of 2 seats. Only Business includes Zero Data Retention.

Two details change the math. Aqua's pricing page offers 70% off Pro and Max with a school email. The iPhone App Store listing shows different in-app prices, with Pro at $12.99 and Max at $39.99, and it covers iPhone only. When you compare, use the web prices from the pricing page, and say which one you quoted.

Lazur starts with a 3-day Pro trial. It needs no credit card, and the clock starts the first time you open the app. Pro is $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power is $120/month, or $96/month annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. After the trial, you choose Pro or Power.

If you pay monthly, the Pro tiers compare like this. Aqua Voice Pro is $12/month and Lazur Pro is $18/month. Aqua's Free plan costs nothing, but it caps you at 1,000 words. Lazur's trial lasts 3 days. If you only dictate a few short notes a day, Aqua's free plan may be enough. If you also want an assistant, the Lazur price buys a different job.
Privacy: what each app stores and sends

Aqua's privacy policy describes two modes. With Privacy Mode off, which is the default, Aqua says it securely stores dictation audio and transcript data on its servers. With Privacy Mode on, it says it does not store your dictation audio or transcript data, except when a dictation is attached to feedback. The policy does not say whether audio or transcripts train AI models. Check that before you dictate client details.

Lazur's rule is simpler to state. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to produce an answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your memory of past requests stays on your Mac. Lazur needs a connection to answer, so plan for that when you travel.

Aqua lists more compliance details. Its llms.txt says it received a SOC 2 Type II report on March 25, 2026, and announced ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification on July 14, 2026. It announced GDPR and HIPAA programs on September 23, 2026, and calls them compliance programs, not certifications. Zero Data Retention is Business only. Max and Business include a BAA signed in the app, and signing turns Privacy Mode on. Lazur's product facts list no BAA and no certification, so ask Lazur before you buy for a regulated team.
Platforms: Mac only, or Mac, Windows and phones

Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Aqua Voice runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel, and on Windows 10 and 11. Its llms.txt also lists iOS 17 and later and Android 10 and later, and calls macOS its primary platform. The latest macOS and Windows build in its changelog is 0.21.4, from October 17, 2026. If you use a Mac at home and a PC at work, Aqua covers both.
How accurate is dictation in each app?

Aqua says its Avalon model scores 97.4% key-term accuracy on the AISpeak-10 test, against 65.1% for Whisper Large v3. That is a vendor claim, and I found no independent test of it. Treat it as a reason to try, not a result. Lazur's product facts do not list an accuracy figure. Your own voice, accent and vocabulary will decide more than any benchmark.

Speed and errors trade off, too. An arXiv study of short messages on touchscreen phones found speech input 2.93 times faster for English, at 153 words per minute against 52 for typing. Speech had a lower corrected error rate during entry, 5.30% against 11.22%. But it left more uncorrected errors in the final text, 1.30% against 0.79%. The study did not test Aqua Voice or any Mac app, so treat it as a warning, not a score.
Edge cases: long text, background speech and no internet

Long text is where dictation tools show their limits. One Product Hunt reviewer reported a long-text paste failure, and other reviewers mention occasional crashes. An aestumanda reviewer said Aqua sometimes transcribes background speech. A SoftOrbits reviewer called its cloud-only design a limit. Lazur listens only while you hold the shortcut, so stray speech between presses matters less. Test both with a long paragraph and a noisy room before you rely on either.
A worked example: replying to a client in Apple Mail

Say you are answering a client in Apple Mail. You need to give a date, name a file and state one next step. With Aqua Voice, you hold Space, dictate the reply and release. The text lands at your cursor. Aqua says Deep Context reads your screen to improve the text, which can help with names already on the page. Still check every name and figure before you send.

With Lazur, you hold fn to dictate the same reply into Mail. Then you hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the attach button is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it, and you click it yourself. If Mail shows a menu you do not know, ask Lazur to walk you through it. It waits for each click, so you move at your own pace.
Can you run both on one Mac?

Yes, but give each app one job. Lazur dictates on hold fn and asks on hold ⌥ ⌘. Aqua's homepage says it is triggered by holding Space, and you can change its keys under Keybindings in its Settings. Space is a key you press all day, so a hold-to-talk setting can fire by accident. If Apple dictation also listens on fn, turn one off in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation. Test a sentence in each app before you rely on either.
Common mistakes when comparing Lazur vs Aqua Voice

items: Comparing App Store prices with web prices. The iPhone listing shows Pro at $12.99, while the pricing page shows $12/month month-to-month.
Assuming Aqua's Free plan is unlimited. It caps you at 1,000 words.
Treating Lazur as only a dictation app. Dictation is included, but the main job is answering and guiding.
Assuming Aqua cannot read your screen. Its Deep Context does, to improve dictation.
Forgetting Privacy Mode. With it off, Aqua stores dictation audio and transcripts on its servers.
Trusting a vendor benchmark as proof for your own voice and vocabulary.

blocks.text: Which one should you pick

items: Pick Aqua Voice if you dictate all day on more than one kind of device.
Pick Aqua Voice if your team needs Business with Zero Data Retention and SSO.
Pick Aqua Voice if a free plan for short notes is enough for now.
Pick Lazur if you want answers about your screen, spoken out loud.
Pick Lazur if you learn new Mac apps and want pointing and step-by-step guidance.
Pick Lazur if you also want timers, reminders and background research by voice.

blocks.text: Some people run both for a while. Keep one dictation app as your default, and use the other for jobs it does better. Test both on the same paragraph before you pay for either.
What to do next

items: Open the Aqua Voice pricing page and check which plan fits how many words you dictate.
Start the Lazur trial from the [download page](/download) and use it for real work for three days.
Dictate the same paragraph in each app, then count the fixes you had to make.
Check Privacy Mode in Aqua before you dictate anything sensitive.
Set your keys so dictation and asking never fire at the same time.

blocks.text: To see how much time voice could save, try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test). For more options, read [Aqua Voice alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/aqua-voice).

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Aqua Voice alternative?
faq.answer: Only if you want more than dictation. Lazur dictates in any Mac app with hold fn, and it also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you step by step. If you need dictation on Windows or phones too, Aqua Voice is the better fit.

faq.question: Which one costs less?
faq.answer: It depends on the plan. Aqua Voice Pro is $12/month month-to-month or $10/month billed annually. Lazur Pro is $18/month or $15/month billed annually. Aqua also has a Free plan capped at 1,000 words. Lazur offers a 3-day trial, then Pro or Power.

faq.question: Does Aqua Voice see my screen?
faq.answer: Aqua's homepage says Deep Context reads your screen, and the Free plan includes it. That screen reading serves dictation. Aqua's pages do not describe it answering questions out loud or pointing at buttons.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Aqua Voice together?
faq.answer: Yes, if their keys do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Aqua's default is holding Space, and you can change it under Keybindings in its Settings. Pick one app for dictation so the two never fight over the same key.

faq.question: Do either of these work offline?
faq.answer: Not really. Aqua's llms.txt says audio is processed in the cloud, and a SoftOrbits reviewer calls it cloud-only with no offline mode. Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers to answer, so it needs a connection too.

faq.question: Which one is better for work data?
faq.answer: Check your own rules first. Aqua offers Privacy Mode, SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and Zero Data Retention on Business. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models, and it looks only while you hold the key. Ask your admin before you send regulated data to either.

verdict: Pick Aqua Voice if your main need is fast dictation on more than one device, or a team plan with Zero Data Retention. Pick Lazur if you want an assistant that sees your Mac screen, answers out loud, points at buttons and guides you through apps. Dictation comes with Lazur, but it is not the headline. Test both on the same paragraph before you pay for either.
